title: Phase 2: authority policy simplification - Tier A/B/C/D, ADR-006, policy tests (AD-006..AD-010)
objective: Replace the per-merge owner-queue posture for ordinary work with the D-010 Section 5 tier model: author ADR-006 (superseding the ADR-005 merge posture while keeping orchestrator-only CLI/git authority), update CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/project-control.md, record the D-004-R721 supersession for Tier A, encode the G6 engineering-vs-publication split (AD-061..AD-063), add deterministic policy tests for every tier, and replay the PRs 143-146 allowlist incident under the new policy.
business_reason: D-010 Section 5 verbatim: replace the owner-approves-nearly-every-merge posture; AD-006..AD-010 and AD-061..AD-063 are explicit directive requirements.
forbidden_paths: tools/project_control.py (behavioral CLI changes require a dedicated defect-lane task)
acceptance_scenarios: AS-1 (executable): ADR-006 defines Tiers A-D exactly per D-010 Section 5, records the D-004-R721 supersession for Tier A ordinary merges, keeps orchestrator-only CLI/git authority (ADR-005 core), and preserves every Section 5.4 hard-deny item and Section 20 hard stop.

AS-2 (executable): tools/test_authority_policy.py encodes the full tier table deterministically - every Tier A action allowed-after-checks, every Tier B class bound to its required specialist review, Tier C queue-and-continue, every Tier D item hard-deny - and the suite is green.
AS-3 (executable): the PRs 143-146 allowlist incident replayed under the new policy yields queue-for-specialist-review, never silent merge (regression test present and green).

AS-4 (executable): CLAUDE.md/rules diffs leave no passage requiring owner approval for ordinary Tier A work; the G6 engineering-acceptance vs publication split (AD-061..AD-063) is recorded; the diff weakens no Tier D item and does not touch the R595 prerequisite (D-010-R104).
risks: Policy text must not drift from D-010 verbatim tiers - reviewer checks quote fidelity.
CLAUDE.md is a governance path: claim requires the cited governance directive (D-010, satisfied).
